reasons: The estimating equations, taper sequence, and bandwidth rule in the theory manuscript match method version 1 exactly.
The uniform consistency theorem assumes sub-Gaussian errors; behavior under heavy-tailed errors is not yet established.
research_attention_at_creation.next_question: Does the taper sequence still control the maximal quantile process error when errors have only a finite fourth moment?

scientific_outcome.conclusion: The tapered quantile estimator is uniformly consistent over a compact coefficient set under sub-Gaussian errors, and its limiting distribution is normal with a sandwich covariance that the paired bootstrap estimates consistently.
scientific_outcome.scope: iid sampling, compact parameter space, sub-Gaussian error tails, and a taper sequence satisfying the stated decay condition.
assumptions: Errors are sub-Gaussian with a uniformly bounded proxy variance.
The taper sequence decays at the rate stated in assumption a2.

theory_scope: Uniform consistency and asymptotic normality of the tapered quantile regression estimator defined by method.example_tapered_quantile version 1, plus a bootstrap covariance validity claim and one resolved counterexample on naive variance estimation.

assumptions.text: The error distribution is sub-Gaussian with proxy variance bounded uniformly over the support of the covariates.
assumptions.scope: All consistency and normality statements in this generation.
assumptions.sensitivity: If the sub-Gaussian bound fails, the maximal inequality in the consistency proof degrades and the uniform rate is no longer guaranteed; normality may survive under a finite fourth moment but this is unverified.

assumptions.text: The taper weights decay at least as fast as the inverse square of the quantile index distance from the boundary.
assumptions.scope: The asymptotic normality statement and the bootstrap validity statement.
assumptions.sensitivity: A slower taper rate inflates the asymptotic variance and can shift the limiting distribution; the bootstrap claim then fails because the bootstrap mimics the stated taper.

statements.text: The tapered quantile estimator is the coefficient vector minimizing the tapered check-loss objective with weights given by the method taper sequence.

justification.summary: Restates the exact calculation defined by method.example_tapered_quantile version 1 in formal notation.

statements.text: For every compact set of coefficient values, the supremum of the estimation error of the tapered quantile estimator converges in probability to zero.
quantifiers: for all coefficient vectors in a compact set
statements.regime: asymptotic as the sample size tends to infinity

justification.summary: A maximal inequality for the tapered empirical process controls the check-loss criterion uniformly, after which identifiability of the population quantile yields consistency.

statements.text: The scaled estimation error converges in distribution to a mean-zero normal law with a sandwich covariance matrix determined by the taper sequence and the error density at the quantile.
quantifiers: for each fixed interior quantile index
statements.regime: asymptotic as the sample size tends to infinity

justification.summary: A Bahadur representation linearizes the estimator; the taper decay condition makes the remainder negligible and a Lindeberg argument gives normality.

statements.text: The paired bootstrap distribution of the scaled estimation error consistently estimates the limiting normal law of the estimator.
statements.regime: asymptotic as the sample size tends to infinity

justification.summary: The bootstrap mimics the Bahadur linearization conditionally on the data, and the taper condition transfers the Lindeberg property to the bootstrap world.

statements.text: The naive inverse-Hessian variance estimator is consistent for the asymptotic variance of the tapered quantile estimator.
quantifiers: for each fixed interior quantile index
statements.regime: asymptotic as the sample size tends to infinity

justification.summary: A two-point covariate design with a boundary-heavy taper makes the inverse-Hessian estimator converge to half the true asymptotic variance, so the claimed consistency fails.

empirical_implications.text: Estimation error of the tapered quantile estimator should decrease toward zero as the sample size grows across repeated simulated datasets.
conditions: iid simulated data with sub-Gaussian errors
coefficient values inside the compact set used in the theory
empirical_implications.observable_or_metric: maximum absolute coefficient error across the quantile grid
empirical_implications.expected_pattern: the error distribution concentrates near zero as sample size increases from 200 to 2000
empirical_implications.falsifying_result: the median error fails to decrease, or the error spread grows, as sample size increases

empirical_implications.text: Bootstrap confidence intervals for the coefficients should attain coverage close to the nominal 95 percent level at interior quantiles.
conditions: paired bootstrap with at least 500 resamples
interior quantile indices away from the taper boundary
empirical_implications.observable_or_metric: empirical coverage of nominal 95 percent bootstrap intervals
empirical_implications.expected_pattern: coverage between 93 and 97 percent across simulation replicates
empirical_implications.falsifying_result: coverage outside 90 to 99 percent at moderate sample sizes

limitations: All results require sub-Gaussian errors; heavy-tailed error behavior is an open item.
The theory covers iid sampling only and says nothing about dependent data.
The counterexample on naive variance estimation removes the simplest standard-error route; only bootstrap inference is currently justified.
